_comment: Hand-curated alias map from TMDB production_companies to a handful of studio labels people actually search for (contract C2 in the v4 plan). TMDB lists every company on a film — often 5-6, including tiny co-financiers and regional/animation/classics sub-labels of the same studio — so without this, 'Warner Bros.' fragments into a dozen near-duplicates. Matching: by numeric TMDB company id first (only ids we are highly confident of, checked against well-known reference films), then by case-insensitive regex on the company name (name_patterns, all anchored with ^ to avoid matching an unrelated company whose name merely contains the string). Everything that matches neither stays raw, keyed 'c:<tmdb_company_id>' with the literal TMDB name — most of the long tail. TO REVIEW: run `python3 src/build_credits.py --report` after an enrichment pass and read the 'top 40 unmapped companies' list — anything there that is clearly one of these studios under a spelling we missed should become a new name_pattern (or, once confirmed against a specific film, a new id) in the matching entry below. Never delete a studio's existing ids without checking they were wrong; do add new ids/patterns freely as evidence accumulates.

studios.label: Warner Bros.
studios.notes: 174 = Warner Bros. Pictures, 12 = New Line Cinema (confident, checked against known New Line titles). Folded in by name pattern: WB/Warner Animation, Turner (WB's TV/library arm), Castle Rock (long-time WB-distributed label). Regional WB entities (e.g. 'Warner Bros. Pictures Germany') are covered by the '^Warner Bros' prefix. Excludes DC Films/DC Studios on purpose: kept as raw 'c:<id>' rather than folded into Warner, since it is a creative brand rather than a distinct production company id and is thin, inconsistent data on TMDB.

studios.label: Sony / Columbia
studios.notes: 5 = Columbia Pictures (confident). TriStar, Screen Gems, Sony Pictures Classics and Sony Pictures Animation are all divisions of Sony Pictures Entertainment and are folded into one 'sony' studio by name pattern rather than id, since their ids are not memorized with confidence. This is a judgment call: someone specifically searching 'TriStar' loses that granularity, but the alternative is four near-identical entries that all mean 'released by Sony'.

studios.label: Universal Pictures
studios.notes: 33 = Universal Pictures (confident). Focus Features is DELIBERATELY KEPT SEPARATE (see the 'focus' entry) rather than merged in, even though it is a Universal specialty division: it is a distinct arthouse brand people search for by name and merging it would erase that signal. Illumination Entertainment (Despicable Me etc.) is also left unmapped/raw on purpose — animation-specific and not requested in the v4 brief; add it here if it turns up often in --report.

studios.label: Focus Features
studios.notes: No id memorized with confidence, so id-matching relies entirely on the anchored name pattern. Kept as its own studio rather than folded into 'universal' — see the note there.

studios.label: Paramount Pictures
studios.notes: 4 = Paramount Pictures (confident).

studios.label: 20th Century Fox
studios.notes: 25 = 20th Century Fox (confident). Disney renamed the studio '20th Century Studios' and 'Fox Searchlight' to 'Searchlight Pictures' after the 2019 acquisition; both old and new names are the same underlying company for our purposes and are folded together under the pre-acquisition label 'fox' since most of the film-history corpus predates the rename.

studios.label: Walt Disney Pictures
studios.notes: 2 = Walt Disney Pictures, 3 = Pixar (both confident). Touchstone Pictures (Disney's former adult-skewing label) is folded in by pattern. Marvel Studios and Lucasfilm are DELIBERATELY KEPT SEPARATE (own entries below) despite common Disney ownership: both are strong creative brands that visitors filter for specifically ('Marvel movies', 'Star Wars/Lucasfilm'), and folding them into 'Disney' would bury exactly the signal a company filter is for. This mirrors how the sister brands are marketed and searched, not the corporate org chart.

studios.label: Marvel Studios
studios.notes: No id memorized with confidence; matched purely by name pattern. Kept separate from Disney — see the note on the 'disney' entry.

studios.label: Lucasfilm
studios.notes: No id memorized with confidence; matched purely by name pattern. Kept separate from Disney — see the note on the 'disney' entry.

studios.label: MGM / United Artists
studios.notes: 21 = Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (confident). United Artists is folded into the same studio by name pattern: MGM acquired UA in 1981 and the two have been run as one library/company for most of the corpus's timeframe. This blurs the pre-1981 distinction between them, a deliberate simplification — split them back out if that period turns out to matter.

studios.notes: No id memorized with confidence; matched purely by name pattern.

studios.label: A24
studios.notes: 41077 = A24 (confident). Name pattern anchored exact-match since 'A24' as a bare prefix could otherwise be too loose.

studios.label: DreamWorks
studios.notes: 7 = DreamWorks Pictures/SKG (confident, live-action). DreamWorks Animation has had a separate corporate history (spun off, later folded into NBCUniversal/Comcast) but is the same audience-facing 'DreamWorks' brand, so it is folded in by name pattern rather than kept apart.
